# Hosts that fail the link check but are not dead.
#
# One extended regular expression per line, matched against the
# `<http_code> <url>` lines the link checker prints. `#` starts a comment.
#
# These used to live as grep literals inside check.yml, which meant the list of
# excuses was editable only by editing CI. That is the same anti-pattern this
# repo catalogues in its own subject: a default nobody can see, charged silently
# to the result. Now it is a file, it is reviewable in a PR, and adding a line
# means saying why.
#
# Every pattern here is a host that rejects automated agents while serving
# humans: a bot-blocked 403/000 is not link rot. Removing a line is the fix for
# a host that has started blocking everything, including browsers.

# Social embeds: these return 400/403 to curl with no JS and no session.
 https://x\.com
 https://twitter\.com

# dev.to serves readers fine and rate-limits anything that looks like a crawler.
 https://dev\.to

# PyPI's JSON/CDN endpoints 403 to curl for these two packages specifically.
 https://pypi\.org/project/(contextwatch|contextlens-profiler)/

# Cognition's blog sits behind a JS challenge for non-browser user agents.
 https://cognition\.com/blog
